neighbours.label: time a person has available to use, read on the time word itself (spare, free or leisure time, a free minute or hour, time off, having enough time or a moment for something); quiet for clock times, how long something lasted, eras ('a hard time'), and rest words without a time noun (a break, the weekend); spare or extra on non-time things (a spare room, extra cash) fires only weakly
fire: In her spare time, she builds model ships from old driftwood.
I finally have some free time this weekend to finish that novel.
Do you have a free minute to look over my report?
Leisure time has grown scarce for parents of young children.
He took a week of time off to help his brother move.
We didn't have enough time to visit the museum before it closed.
Could you spare a moment to sign this card for Mr. Hale?
If I get a free hour tomorrow, I'll call the plumber.
quiet: In her spare room, she keeps model ships made from old driftwood.
I finally finished that novel at nine o'clock this weekend.
The meeting lasted forty minutes and covered the whole report.
The war years were a hard time for families in the valley.
He took a long break to help his brother move.
The museum closes at five thirty on weekdays.
Could you sign this card for Mr. Hale by Friday?
The flight took three hours longer than expected.
